\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{وطن} (vatan)}{وطن (vatan)}]{\ur{وطن} (vatan) — a homeland}

\label{lesson:UR-C400-vatan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for forbidden, then the Urdu for to put on board.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{وطن}}
\textbf{\ur{وطن}} — \emph{vatan} — \textquotedblleft{}a homeland\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرا} \ur{وطن} \ur{یہاں} \ur{سے} \ur{دور} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā vatan yahāṅ se dūr hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My homeland is a long way from here.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{وطن}} (\emph{vatan}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{waṭan}, \textquotedblleft{}a dwelling place, a homeland\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vatan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vatan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merā vatan yahāṅ se dūr hai.} — My homeland is a long way from here.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for forbidden, then the Urdu for to put on board, then say \emph{vatan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{وطن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A homeland\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پردیس} (pardes)}{پردیس (pardes)}]{\ur{پردیس} (pardes) — a foreign land}

\label{lesson:UR-C400-pardes}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to put on board, then the Urdu for a homeland.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پردیس}}
\textbf{\ur{پردیس}} — \emph{pardes} — \textquotedblleft{}a foreign land\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Masculine.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اجنبی} (ajnabī)}{اجنبی (ajnabī)}]{\ur{اجنبی} (ajnabī) — a stranger}

\label{lesson:UR-C400-ajnabi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a homeland, then the Urdu for a foreign land.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اجنبی}}
\textbf{\ur{اجنبی}} — \emph{ajnabī} — \textquotedblleft{}a stranger\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پردیس} \ur{میں} \ur{سب} \ur{لوگ} \ur{اجنبی} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pardes meṅ sab log ajnabī the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Abroad, everyone was a stranger.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اجنبی}} (\emph{ajnabī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ajnabī}, \textquotedblleft{}foreign, a stranger\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گزارنا} (guzārnā)}{گزارنا (guzārnā)}]{\ur{گزارنا} (guzārnā) — to spend (time)}

\label{lesson:UR-C400-guzarna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a foreign land, then the Urdu for a stranger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گزارنا}}
\textbf{\ur{گزارنا}} — \emph{guzārnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to spend (time)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سارا} \ur{نے} \ur{پردیس} \ur{میں} \ur{دو} \ur{سال} \ur{گزارے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sārā ne pardes meṅ do sāl guzāre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Sara spent two years abroad.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{وہاں} \ur{ایک} \ur{ہفتہ} \ur{گزارا}, \emph{us ne vahāṅ ek haftā guzārā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گزارنا}} (\emph{guzārnā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{guzār}, \textquotedblleft{}a passing\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ur{گزشتہ}}, \textquotedblleft{}last, previous\textquotedblright{}, is a time that has passed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guzārnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guzārnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sārā ne pardes meṅ do sāl guzāre.} — Sara spent two years abroad.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a foreign land, then the Urdu for a stranger, then say \emph{guzārnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{گزارنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To spend (time)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{واپسی} (vāpasī)}{واپسی (vāpasī)}]{\ur{واپسی} (vāpasī) — a return; the way back}

\label{lesson:UR-C400-vapasi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a stranger, then the Urdu for to spend (time).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{واپسی}}
\textbf{\ur{واپسی}} — \emph{vāpasī} — \textquotedblleft{}a return; the way back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہماری} \ur{واپسی} \ur{اگلے} \ur{ہفتے} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hamārī vāpasī agle hafte hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We come back next week.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{واپسی}} (\emph{vāpasī}) is built on \emph{vāpas}, \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{vāpas}, with the ending \emph{-ī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
